newsitem.title: MEXICO: Swiss prosecutor to question Mexico's Raul Salinas.
newsitem.headline: Swiss prosecutor to question Mexico's Raul Salinas.

text.p: Switzerland's chief prosecutor has arrived in Mexico to question the brother of former President Carlos Salinas about a multi-million dollar secret bank account in Switzerland, officials said on Monday.

Prosecutor Carla del Ponte and Valentin Roschacher, head of the Swiss anti-drug police, planned to interrogate Raul Salinas on Monday about the origin of $84 million stashed in the account, said a Mexican government official.
The official, who wished to remain anonymous, said the Swiss officials arrived in Mexico City late on Sunday.
Raul Salinas was arrested in early 1995 on charges of plotting the murder of a top politician and of illicit enrichment.
He also was recently charged by Mexican authorities with money laundering. He is currently in a maximum-security jail just outside Mexico City.

The fortune was discovered in September 1995 when Raul Salinas' wife tried to withdraw the funds. Since then, Swiss and Mexican officials have been investigating whether or not the money was laundered from the illegal drug trade.
Salinas has denied the charges and said the money was from legitimate business in Mexico.

Salinas is alleged to have amassed a fortune while serving as an official during part of his brother's 1988-1994 term. Carlos Salinas fled Mexico soon after his term ended and now lives in self-imposed exile in Ireland.

It is the third time Swiss investigators have come to Mexico to question Raul Salinas. Mexican newspapers reported the Swiss investigators were in the United States for three days last week, meeting with officials from the Justice Department and Drug Enforcement Administration.

Drugs-related corruption in Mexico has become a flashpoint in its relations with the United States, where most of the illegal drugs are headed. Despite recent drugs scandals in Mexico, the United States still officially considers Mexico an ally in the drugs war.
